target: Shopify Files — normalised ingredient selector tiles
decided_by: Malcolm, 2026-08-25 — make the selector tiles all show the product at the same size; serums to the PDRN bottle, jars to the Copper Peptide night cream pot
note:
Nine re-framed selector tiles. Product scale was ranging 47%-84% of frame because the nine shots came from nine different shoots, so the rows read as ragged.

NOTHING IS RESAMPLED. The product is never scaled - only the canvas around it changes, so the pixels a visitor sees are the originals. New canvas edge = product_height / target_fraction; the canvas grows to make a product relatively smaller and is cropped in to make it larger.

FINDING THE PRODUCT WAS THE HARD PART. Brightness thresholding does not work: a frosted white bottle on a white sweep has almost no brightness contrast, and that approach measured the acetyl bottle at 18% of frame against a true 80%. The silhouette comes from gradient magnitude instead - the product has sharp edges, the studio background only smooth ones - closed solid, holes filled, largest blob kept. The glutathione frame needed a more sensitive threshold than the rest and carries its own value.

EDGE REPLICATION, NOT FLAT FILL. The first build sampled a median background colour and filled with it, which left a visible rectangle on five of the nine tiles where the fill butted against the original - these sweeps are gradients, not white. Replicating the border outward carries the gradient instead and the join has nothing to show.

Every box was checked by eye against a drawn overlay before anything was written, which is how the two mis-detections were caught rather than published.
